questions.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence “Nowadays more and more people choose to live an environmentally friendly lifestyle.” You can make comments, cite examples, or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
questions.correctAnswer:
Nowadays more and more people choose to live an environmentally friendly lifestyle. This change shows that environmental protection is increasingly seen as a daily responsibility rather than a distant public issue. Ordinary decisions can reduce waste and encourage wider improvements.

An environmentally friendly lifestyle begins with consuming resources thoughtfully. Carrying a reusable bottle, choosing public transport when practical and avoiding unnecessary purchases are simple examples. These actions become more effective when they form consistent habits. In my own experience, planning meals before shopping helped my family waste less food and spend less money. Such benefits make sustainable choices easier to maintain. However, individuals also need convenient facilities and clear information. Reliable recycling systems and safe walking routes allow good intentions to become practical behavior.

We should therefore combine personal effort with support from communities and businesses. People can start with changes suited to their circumstances and gradually improve. When responsible habits are made convenient and worthwhile, they can spread beyond a few enthusiastic individuals and contribute to a healthier environment for everyone.

questions.prompt: Some children on the remote islands won't eat their meals because they are fed cheap junk food.
questions.passage:
The Doctor Will Skype You Now

A) Fazila is a young woman that has been dealing with eczema(湿疹), a common skin condition, for the past five years, but never got it treated. The nearest hospital is an hour away, by boat and bus, and her skin condition didn't seem serious enough to make the trek, so she ignored it—until a new technology brought the doctor to her. Fazila lives on one of the remote river islands in northern Bangladesh. These islands are low-lying, temporary sand islands that are continuously formed and destroyed through sand buildup and erosion. They are home to over six million people, who face repeated displacement from flooding and erosion—which may be getting worse because of climate change—and a range of health risks, including poor nutrition, malaria(疟疾) and other water-borne diseases.

B) The most dangerous thing for these remote island dwellers is land erosion. The second is lack of access to medical supplies and doctors. There are no doctors within miles, and while child mortality and maternal death have gone down in the rest of the country, this is not the case for the islands. The medical situation is so bad that it really takes away from the quality of their life. Yet for many island inhabitants—some of Bangladesh's poorest—paying for health care is a costly ordeal. Victims of erosion lose their houses, agricultural land and jobs as farmers, fishermen and day laborers. Though government hospitals are free, many people hesitate to go, citing long commutes, endless lines and questionable diagnoses.
